arxiv-2106-09052.title: The quantum mass gap of extremal black holes
arxiv-2106-09052.creator: Shahar Hod
arxiv-2106-09052.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shahar Hod. Using sophisticated string theory calculations, Maldacena and Susskind have intriguingly shown that near-extremal black holes are characterized by a finite mass gap above the corresponding zero-temperature (extremal) black-hole configuration. In the present compact paper we explicitly prove that the minimum energy gap ℰ gap = ℏ 2 / M 3 {\cal E}_{\text{gap}}=\hbar^{2}/M^{3} , which characterizes the mass spectra of near-extremal charged Reissner-Nordström black holes, can be inferred from a simple semi-classical analysis.

arxiv-2312-00803.title: InceptionCaps: A Performant Glaucoma Classification Model for Data-scarce Environment
arxiv-2312-00803.creator: Gyanendar Manohar, Ruairi O’Reilly
arxiv-2312-00803.description: Abstract Glaucoma is an irreversible ocular disease and is the second leading cause of visual disability worldwide. Slow vision loss and the asymptomatic nature of the disease make its diagnosis challenging. Early detection is crucial for preventing irreversible blindness. Ophthalmologists primarily use retinal fundus images as a non-invasive screening method.

arxiv-2406-04274.title: Self-Play with Adversarial Critic: Provable and Scalable Offline Alignment for Language Models
arxiv-2406-04274.creator: Xiang Ji, Sanjeev Kulkarni, Mengdi Wang, Tengyang Xie
arxiv-2406-04274.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Xiang Ji, Sanjeev Kulkarni, Mengdi Wang, Tengyang Xie. This work studies the challenge of aligning large language models (LLMs) with offline preference data. We focus on alignment by Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) in particular. While popular preference optimization methods exhibit good empirical performance in practice, they are not theoretically guaranteed to converge to the optimal policy and can provably fail when the data coverage is sparse by classical offline reinforcement learning (RL) results.

arxiv-2407-18634.title: Turbulent transport regimes in the presence of an X-point magnetic configuration
arxiv-2407-18634.creator: Fabio Moretti, Nakia Carlevaro, Francesco Cianfrani, Giovanni Montani
arxiv-2407-18634.description: Abstract We analyze the transport properties of the two-dimensional electrostatic turbulence characterizing the edge of a Tokamak device from the study of test particles motion (passive fluid tracers) following the 𝐄 × 𝐁 \mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B} drift. We perform statistical tests on the tracer population in order to assess both the magnitude and the main features of transport.

arxiv-2412-20842.title: Revisiting the flaring activity in early 2015 of BL Lacertae object S5 0716+714
arxiv-2412-20842.creator: Zhihao Ouyang, Hubing Xiao, Marina Manganaro, Shangchun Xie, Jingyu Wu, Jianzhen Chen, Rui Xue, Gege Wang, Shaohua Zhang, Junhui Fan
arxiv-2412-20842.description: Abstract In this work, we analyzed multi-wavelength data of the BL Lac object S5 0716+714 to investigate its emission mechanisms during a flaring state observed in early 2015. We examined the temporal behavior and broadband spectral energy distributions (SEDs) during the flare. The size of the γ \gamma -ray emission region was estimated based on the variability timescale.

arxiv-2510-09541.title: SPG: Sandwiched Policy Gradient for Masked Diffusion Language Models
arxiv-2510-09541.creator: Chenyu Wang, Paria Rashidinejad, DiJia Su, Song Jiang, Sid Wang, Siyan Zhao, Cai Zhou, Shannon Zejiang Shen, Feiyu Chen, Tommi Jaakkola, Yuandong Tian, Bo Liu
arxiv-2510-09541.description: Abstract Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) are emerging as an efficient alternative to autoregressive models due to their ability to decode multiple tokens in parallel. However, aligning dLLMs with human preferences or task-specific rewards via reinforcement learning (RL) is challenging because their intractable log-likelihood precludes the direct application of standard policy gradient methods.

arxiv-2510-12264.title: T 3 : Reducing Belief Deviation in Reinforcement Learning for Active Reasoning
arxiv-2510-12264.creator: Deyu Zou, Yongqiang Chen, Jianxiang Wang, Haochen Yang, Mufei Li, James Cheng, Pan Li, Yu Gong
arxiv-2510-12264.description: Abstract Active reasoning requires large language models (LLMs) to interact with external sources and strategically gather information to solve problems. Central to this process is belief tracking : maintaining a coherent understanding of the problem state and the missing information toward the solution.

pmc-11456902.title: The hot spots and global trends of prevention and treatment in postoperative delirium (POD) from 2004 to 2023: A bibliometric analysis
pmc-11456902.creator: Changshuo Jiang, Zijun Tian, Ming Jiang, Chenyang Xu, Mingjie Mao, Shanwu Feng, Hongmei Yuan
pmc-11456902.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundPostoperative delirium (POD) is an acute postoperative syndrome of the central nervous system that seriously affects the prognosis of patients. Many vital advances have been made in the study of the management of POD. We conducted a bibliometric analysis of research on the prevention and treatment of POD over the past 20 years to consolidate current research focal points and emerging trends in this domain.MethodsWe searched the Web of Science Core Collection database for literature published between 2004 and 2023.

pmc-11499583.title: Sepsis-Inducing Leukocytoclastic Vasculitis Resistant to Steroid Therapy: A Case Report
pmc-11499583.creator: Jena Jacobs, Joseph Norman, Stephen Verral
pmc-11499583.description: A 34-year-old White male presented with a persistent rash on the lower extremities characterized by erythema, liquid drainage, and severe burning pain. Initially misattributed to contact dermatitis, the condition worsened despite treatment with prednisone and doxycycline. Leukocytoclastic vasculitis (LCV) was confirmed via punch biopsy. The patient’s treatment involved conservative measures, systemic prednisone therapy, doxycycline, and later adjunctive dapsone.

pmc-11508692.title: Human iPSCs from Aged Donors Retain Their Mitochondrial Aging Signature
pmc-11508692.creator: Imane Lejri, Zameel Cader, Amandine Grimm, Anne Eckert, Alessandra Ferramosca
pmc-11508692.description: Aging represents the leading risk factor for developing neurodegenerative disorders. One of the nine hallmarks of aging is mitochondrial dysfunction. Age-related mitochondrial alterations have been shown to affect mitochondrial energy metabolism, reduction-oxidation homeostasis, and mitochondrial dynamics. Previous reports have shown that induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from aged donors do not keep the aging signature at the transcriptomic level.

pmc-11574923.title: Cell-Free Systems Biology: Characterizing Central Metabolism of Clostridium thermocellum with a Three-Enzyme Cascade Reaction
pmc-11574923.creator: S Bilal Jilani, Markus Alahuhta, Yannick J Bomble, Daniel G Olson
pmc-11574923.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Genetic approaches have been traditionally used to understand microbial metabolism, but this process can be slow in nonmodel organisms due to limited genetic tools. An alternative approach is to study metabolism directly in the cell lysate. This avoids the need for genetic tools and is routinely used to study individual enzymatic reactions but is not generally used to study systems-level properties of metabolism.

pmc-12646238.title: Advancing stochastic 3-SAT solvers by dissipating oversatisfied constraints
pmc-12646238.creator: Joachim Schwardt, Jan Carl Budich
pmc-12646238.description: SignificanceHard decision problems, in computational complexity theory known as NP-complete, are of universal importance. From a conceptual perspective, an efficient solution to one such complete problem is tantamount to solving any other in the wide class of efficiently verifiable (NP) problems. Moreover, paradigmatic examples such as the Boolean satisfiability problem 3-SAT have ubiquitous applications ranging from circuit design to logistics.

pmc-12839285.title: The Current State of Mock Circulatory Loop Applications in Aortic and Cardiovascular Research: A Scoping Review
pmc-12839285.creator: Felix E. N. Osinga, Nesar A. Hasami, Jasper F. de Kort, Emma-Lena Maris, Maurizio Domanin, Martina Schembri, Alessandro Caimi, Michele Conti, Constantijn E. V. B. Hazenberg, Ferdinando Auricchio, Jorg L. de Bruin, Joost A. van Herwaarden, Santi Trimarchi
pmc-12839285.description: Background: Mock circulatory loops (MCLs) are benchtop experimental platforms that reproduce key features of the human cardiovascular system, providing a safe, controlled, and reproducible environment for haemodynamic investigation. This scoping review aims to systematically map the current landscape of MCLs used for aortic simulation and identify major areas of application.

pmc-13221328.title: Operative timing and surgical complexity in hand trauma: a multicenter analysis of replantation and non-replantation centers in Germany
pmc-13221328.creator: Antek Nicklas, Patrick Will Marks, Adrian Dragu, Hannah Schmidt, Andre Rotärmel, HandTraumaRegister DGH
pmc-13221328.description: BackgroundHand injuries are common traumatic conditions that often require specialized surgical care. Differences in hospital structures and levels of specialization may influence the timeliness and complexity of treatment. This study evaluates quality of care across different hospital types, focusing on time-to-skin-incision and surgical management of finger and hand injuries.

pmc-13629669.creator: Georgia A. Pilkington, Oliver S. Hammond, Erik Bergendal, Anna Oleshkevych, Stuart J. Brown, Sichao Li, Andrew Nelson, Liliana de Campo, Rebecca Welbourn, Akepati Bhaskar Reddy, Manishkumar R. Shimpi, Sergei Glavatskih, Anja-Verena Mudring, Mark W. Rutland
